# GMP recipes

Complete schemas from the GMP repository `examples/` (each one compiles and runs there), with the C++ that uses them.
Pick the closest one, copy it, and adapt it.

Contents:
1. Framed binary link: sync, header, length, CRC, several message types, streaming
2. Text protocol (NMEA 0183): tokens, XOR checksum, optional fields
3. CAN payload with bit-packed Intel signals, and a fixed-size framed link
4. I2C sensor with a CRC after every word, unit conversions and a computed value
5. Serial link where 0x80 is a reserved sync byte (byte stuffing)
6. Custom field codec and custom checksum in C++

## 1. Framed binary link (length-prefixed, CRC, several messages)

**Use when:** a UART / TCP / radio link with a sync word, a header holding a message id and a length, and a CRC.

```yaml
# examples/binary_telemetry/telemetry.yaml
# Length-prefixed binary link with sync word, CRC, message-type selection and a conditional nested message.
schema_version: 1
namespace: demo
defaults: { endian: big }

enums:
  Mode: { type: u8, values: { idle: 0, run: 1, fault: 2 } }

messages:
  Fault:
    fields:
      - { name: code, type: u16 }
      - { name: temperature, type: i16, scale: 0.1, unit: degC }

  Status:
    type_id: 1
    fields:
      - { name: uptime_s, type: u32 }
      - { name: voltage, type: u16, scale: 0.001, unit: V }
      - name: state
        type: bits
        fields:
          - { name: armed, bits: 1 }
          - { name: mode, bits: 2, enum: Mode }
          - { pad: 5 }
      - { name: fault, type: Fault, when: "state.mode == Mode.fault" }

  Samples:
    type_id: 2
    fields:
      - { name: channel, type: u8 }
      - { name: count, type: u8 }
      - { name: values, type: array, of: i16, count: count, max: 64 }

protocols:
  Link:
    header:
      - { name: id, type: u8 }
      - { name: length, type: u16 }
    framing:
      type: length_prefixed
      sync: [0xAA, 0x55]
      length: { field: length, covers: body }
    checksum: { algo: crc16_ccitt }
    message_type: { field: id }
    messages: [Status, Samples]
```

- `message_type: { field: id }` picks the message by its `type_id`; the protocol fills `id` and `length` on encode.
- `when:` makes `fault` an `std::optional` that exists only in fault mode.
- The stream parser skips noise (`BadSync`) and corrupt frames (`BadChecksum`) and keeps going.

```cpp
// Encode a few frames, add line noise, and recover the messages with the stream parser.
#include <cstdio>
#include <vector>

#include "telemetry.gmp.hpp"

int main() {
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> wire;
    auto append = [&](const auto& msg) {
        std::array<std::uint8_t, demo::Link::max_frame> buf{};
        if (auto n = demo::Link::encode(msg, buf)) wire.insert(wire.end(), buf.begin(), buf.begin() + static_cast<std::ptrdiff_t>(*n));
    };

    demo::Status ok;
    ok.uptime_s = 3600;
    ok.set_voltage_scaled(12.6);
    ok.state.armed = true;
    ok.state.mode = demo::Mode::run;
    append(ok);

    wire.insert(wire.end(), {0x13, 0x37, 0xAA});  // line noise

    demo::Samples s;
    s.channel = 3;
    s.values = {100, -100, 250};  // `count` is filled in automatically
    append(s);

    demo::Status bad = ok;
    bad.state.mode = demo::Mode::fault;
    bad.fault = demo::Fault{0x0042, 875};
    append(bad);

    // The parser stores the handler, so the receive path below only passes bytes.
    // (Alternatives: demo::Link::Stream<> with feed(bytes, handler), or CallbackStream with on<&App::fn>(app).)
    auto parser = demo::Link::make_stream(gmsg::overloaded{
        [](const demo::StatusView& v) {
            std::printf("Status  uptime=%us voltage=%.3fV mode=%s", static_cast<unsigned>(v.uptime_s()), v.voltage_scaled(),
                        demo::to_string(v.state().mode).data());
            if (auto f = v.fault()) std::printf(" fault=0x%04X temp=%.1fC", f->code(), f->temperature_scaled());
            std::printf("\n");
        },
        [](const demo::SamplesView& v) {
            // gmsg::println dumps every field (enum names, units, nested messages); see README "Printing"
            gmsg::println(v, stdout, {.style = gmsg::PrintStyle::single_line});
        },
        [](const gmsg::FrameError& e) {
            std::printf("dropped %zu byte(s): %s\n", e.data.size(), gmsg::to_string(e.error).data());
        },
    });
    // Deliver the stream in awkward 5-byte chunks, as a UART driver might.
    const gmsg::bytes_view all(wire);
    for (std::size_t off = 0; off < all.size(); off += 5)
        parser.feed(all.subspan(off, std::min<std::size_t>(5, all.size() - off)));

    const auto& st = parser.stats();
    std::printf("frames=%u errors=%u skipped=%u\n", static_cast<unsigned>(st.frames),
                static_cast<unsigned>(st.frame_errors), static_cast<unsigned>(st.bytes_skipped));
    return 0;
}
```


## 2. Text protocol: NMEA 0183

**Use when:** ASCII sentences such as `$GPGGA,...*47\r\n`: delimited frames, comma-separated tokens, hex checksum.

```yaml
# examples/nmea_text/nmea.yaml
schema_version: 1
namespace: nav::nmea
defaults: { format: text, separator: "," }

enums:
  FixQuality:
    type: u8
    values: { invalid: 0, gps: 1, dgps: 2 }

messages:
  GGA:
    type_id: GPGGA
    doc: Global positioning system fix data.
    fields:
      - { name: utc_time, type: f64, precision: 2, width: 9 }
      - { name: latitude, type: f64, precision: 4, width: 9, optional: true }
      - { name: lat_hemi, type: char, optional: true }
      - { name: longitude, type: f64, precision: 4, width: 10, optional: true }
      - { name: lon_hemi, type: char, optional: true }
      - { name: quality, type: FixQuality }
      - { name: satellites, type: u8, width: 2 }
      - { name: hdop, type: f32, precision: 1, optional: true }
      - { name: altitude, type: f64, precision: 1, optional: true }
      - { name: altitude_unit, type: char, optional: true }
      - { pad: 4 }
  TXT:
    type_id: GPTXT
    fields:
      - { name: total, type: u8, width: 2 }
      - { name: number, type: u8, width: 2 }
      - { name: severity, type: u8, width: 2 }
      - { name: text, type: string, max: 61 }

protocols:
  Nmea:
    framing: { type: delimited, start: "$", end: "\r\n", max_frame: 82 }
    checksum: { algo: xor8, separator: "*" }
    message_type: { token: 0 }
    messages: [GGA, TXT]
```

- `format: text` in `defaults`; each field is one token, `{ pad: 4 }` skips four tokens.
- `message_type: { token: 0 }` matches the first token (`GPGGA`) against `type_id`.
- Text view accessors parse on demand and return `gmsg::Result<T>` (optional fields: `Result<std::optional<T>>`).

```cpp
// Parse NMEA 0183 sentences (text protocol, XOR checksum, optional fields) and encode one.
#include <cstdio>
#include <string_view>

#include "nmea.gmp.hpp"

namespace nm = nav::nmea;

int main() {
    constexpr std::string_view log =
        "$GPGGA,123519,4807.038,N,01131.000,E,1,08,0.9,545.4,M,46.9,M,,*47\r\n"
        "$GPGGA,123520,4807.038,N,01131.000,E,1,08,0.9,545.4,M,46.9,M,,*00\r\n"  // bad checksum
        "$GPTXT,01,01,02,ANTSTATUS=OK*3B\r\n"
        "$GPGGA,000000,,,,,0,00,,,,,,,*66\r\n";

    nm::Nmea::Stream<> parser;
    parser.feed(gmsg::as_bytes(log.data(), log.size()),
                gmsg::overloaded{
                    [](const nm::GGAView& g) {
                        // Text views parse lazily: each accessor returns gmsg::Result<T>.
                        std::printf("GGA time=%.0f quality=%s sats=%u", g.utc_time().value_or(0.0),
                                    nm::to_string(g.quality().value_or(nm::FixQuality::invalid)).data(),
                                    static_cast<unsigned>(g.satellites().value_or(0)));
                        auto lat = g.latitude();  // Result<optional<double>>: optional field
                        if (lat && *lat) std::printf(" lat=%.3f", **lat);
                        else std::printf(" (no fix)");
                        std::printf("\n");
                    },
                    [](const nm::TXTView& t) {
                        std::printf("TXT \"%.*s\"\n", static_cast<int>(t.text().size()), t.text().data());
                    },
                    [](const gmsg::FrameError& e) { std::printf("rejected: %s\n", gmsg::to_string(e.error).data()); },
                });

    nm::TXT txt;
    txt.total = 1;
    txt.number = 1;
    txt.severity = 2;
    txt.text = "HELLO";
    std::array<std::uint8_t, nm::Nmea::max_frame> out{};
    if (auto n = nm::Nmea::encode(txt, out))
        std::printf("encoded: %.*s", static_cast<int>(*n), reinterpret_cast<const char*>(out.data()));
    return 0;
}
```


## 3. CAN payload with bit-packed signals

**Use when:** a DBC-style CAN frame (Intel `@1` = `lsb_first`, little endian), or any register map with sub-byte fields.

```yaml
# examples/bitpacked_can/can.yaml
schema_version: 1
namespace: vehicle::can
defaults: { endian: little, bit_order: lsb_first }

enums:
  Gear: { type: u8, values: { park: 0, reverse: 1, neutral: 2, drive: 3 } }

messages:
  EngineData:
    doc: 8-byte CAN payload with Intel (lsb_first) signals.
    fields:
      - name: signals
        type: bits
        fields:
          - { name: rpm, bits: 14, type: u16, scale: 0.5 }
          - { name: gear, bits: 2, enum: Gear }
          - { name: coolant, bits: 8, type: u8, offset: -40 }
          - { name: throttle, bits: 10, type: u16, scale: 0.1 }
          - { pad: 6 }
          - { name: counter, bits: 4 }
          - { name: version, bits: 4, const: 1 }
          - { name: flags, bits: 16, type: u16 }

  Sensor:
    type_id: 1
    fields:
      - { name: temp, type: i16, scale: 0.01 }
      - { name: humidity, type: u8 }

protocols:
  Can:
    framing: { type: none }
    messages: [EngineData]

  FixedLink:
    endian: big
    header: [ { name: id, type: u8 } ]
    framing: { type: fixed, sync: 0xA5A5, size: 10 }
    checksum: { algo: { crc: { width: 8, poly: 0x1D, init: 0xFF, xorout: 0xFF } } }
    message_type: { field: id }
    messages: [Sensor]
```

- `framing: { type: none }`: the 8 data bytes are the frame (the CAN controller already framed it).
- Bit fields take `type`, `enum`, `scale`, `offset` and `const`; `{ pad: N }` reserves bits.
- `FixedLink` shows fixed-size framing with a 2-byte sync word and an inline CRC definition.

```cpp
// Decode a bit-packed (Intel / lsb_first) CAN payload in place, and build one from values.
#include <cstdio>

#include "can.gmp.hpp"

namespace vc = vehicle::can;

int main() {
    // As received from a CAN controller: 8 data bytes.
    const std::array<std::uint8_t, 8> payload{0xE8, 0xC3, 0x82, 0x00, 0x02, 0x19, 0xEF, 0xBE};

    auto view = vc::EngineDataView::from(payload);
    if (!view) {
        std::printf("invalid frame: %s\n", gmsg::to_string(view.error()).data());
        return 1;
    }
    const auto s = view->signals();
    std::printf("rpm=%.1f gear=%s coolant=%.0fC throttle=%.1f%% counter=%u flags=0x%04X\n", s.rpm_scaled(),
                vc::to_string(s.gear).data(), s.coolant_scaled(), s.throttle_scaled(), s.counter, s.flags);

    vc::EngineData out;
    out.signals.rpm = static_cast<std::uint16_t>(3000 / 0.5);
    out.signals.gear = vc::Gear::drive;
    out.signals.coolant = static_cast<std::uint8_t>(95 + 40);
    std::array<std::uint8_t, 8> frame{};
    if (auto n = out.encode(frame)) {
        std::printf("encoded:");
        for (std::size_t i = 0; i < *n; ++i) std::printf(" %02X", frame[i]);
        std::printf("\n");
    }
    return 0;
}
```


## 4. I2C sensor with per-word CRCs (Sensirion SHT4x)

**Use when:** a sensor datasheet where each 16-bit word is followed by its own CRC-8, with conversion formulas and commands.

```yaml
# examples/sensirion_sht4x/sht4x.yaml
# Sensirion SHT4x relative humidity & temperature sensor (SHT40/41/43/45).
# Source: SHT4x datasheet, version 5 (January 2023), sections 4.3 - 4.7.
#
# The sensor is an I2C slave at 0x44 (SHT4x-A), 0x45 (SHT4x-B) or 0x46 (SHT40-C). I2C addressing,
# the R/W bit and ACK/NACK are handled by your bus driver; this schema describes the bytes that are
# written to and read from the sensor:
#
#   1. write one command byte                    -> encode a command message (e.g. MeasureHighPrecision)
#   2. wait for the command (see `doc` below)    -> the sensor NACKs reads until it is done
#   3. read 6 bytes                              -> decode with MeasurementResponse or SerialNumberResponse,
#                                                   depending on the command that was sent
#
# Every 16-bit word the sensor sends is followed by a CRC-8 (poly 0x31, init 0xFF, no reflection,
# xorout 0x00; CRC(0xBEEF) = 0x92). That is the CRC-8/NRSC-5 preset, applied per field with `crc:`.
schema_version: 1
namespace: sensirion::sht4x
defaults: { endian: big }

messages:
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Commands (master -> sensor): one byte each (datasheet Table 8)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  MeasureHighPrecision:
    doc: Measure T & RH with high repeatability. Read a Measurement after 8.3 ms (max).
    fields: [ { name: command, type: u8, const: 0xFD } ]
  MeasureMediumPrecision:
    doc: Measure T & RH with medium repeatability. Read a Measurement after 4.5 ms (max).
    fields: [ { name: command, type: u8, const: 0xF6 } ]
  MeasureLowPrecision:
    doc: Measure T & RH with low repeatability. Read a Measurement after 1.6 ms (max).
    fields: [ { name: command, type: u8, const: 0xE0 } ]
  ReadSerialNumber:
    doc: Read the unique serial number. Read a SerialNumber next.
    fields: [ { name: command, type: u8, const: 0x89 } ]
  SoftReset:
    doc: Soft reset; the sensor is idle again after 1 ms (max). No response.
    fields: [ { name: command, type: u8, const: 0x94 } ]
  Heater200mW1s:
    doc: Heater at 200 mW for 1 s, then a high-precision measurement. Read a Measurement after 1.1 s (max).
    fields: [ { name: command, type: u8, const: 0x39 } ]
  Heater200mW100ms:
    doc: Heater at 200 mW for 0.1 s, then a high-precision measurement. Read a Measurement after 0.11 s (max).
    fields: [ { name: command, type: u8, const: 0x32 } ]
  Heater110mW1s:
    doc: Heater at 110 mW for 1 s, then a high-precision measurement. Read a Measurement after 1.1 s (max).
    fields: [ { name: command, type: u8, const: 0x2F } ]
  Heater110mW100ms:
    doc: Heater at 110 mW for 0.1 s, then a high-precision measurement. Read a Measurement after 0.11 s (max).
    fields: [ { name: command, type: u8, const: 0x24 } ]
  Heater20mW1s:
    doc: Heater at 20 mW for 1 s, then a high-precision measurement. Read a Measurement after 1.1 s (max).
    fields: [ { name: command, type: u8, const: 0x1E } ]
  Heater20mW100ms:
    doc: Heater at 20 mW for 0.1 s, then a high-precision measurement. Read a Measurement after 0.11 s (max).
    fields: [ { name: command, type: u8, const: 0x15 } ]

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Responses (sensor -> master)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Measurement:
    doc: |-
      Response to the measure and heater commands (datasheet 4.3, 4.6).
      Humidity is not cropped: values slightly below 0 or above 100 %RH are possible; clamp if needed.
    fields:
      - name: temperature
        type: u16
        crc: crc8_nrsc5
        scale: 0.0026703288319218739     # 175 / 65535
        offset: -45
        unit: degC
        conversions:
          degf: { scale: 0.0048065918974593731, offset: -49, unit: degF }   # 315 / 65535
      - name: humidity
        type: u16
        crc: crc8_nrsc5
        scale: 0.0019073777370870527     # 125 / 65535
        offset: -6
        unit: "%RH"
  SerialNumber:
    doc: Response to ReadSerialNumber (datasheet 4.7) - two 16-bit words, each followed by its CRC.
    fields:
      - { name: serial_high, type: u16, crc: crc8_nrsc5 }
      - { name: serial_low, type: u16, crc: crc8_nrsc5 }
    computed:
      serial:                                   # serial() on struct and view, set_serial() on the struct
        type: u32
        value: "(serial_high << 16) | serial_low"

protocols:
  # The response bytes do not identify themselves, so each response layout is its own protocol;
  # decode with the one matching the command you sent.
  MeasurementResponse:
    doc: 6 bytes read after a measure or heater command.
    framing: { type: fixed, size: 6 }
    messages: [Measurement]
  SerialNumberResponse:
    doc: 6 bytes read after ReadSerialNumber.
    framing: { type: fixed, size: 6 }
    messages: [SerialNumber]
```

- `crc: crc8_nrsc5` on a field = checksum stored right after that value (not a protocol checksum).
- `scale` / `offset` implement the datasheet formula; `conversions` adds a second unit (°F).
- `computed:` joins `serial_high` / `serial_low`; `set_serial()` splits it back automatically.
- Each 1-byte command is its own message with a `const` field. `examples/sensirion_sht4x/sht4x_enum.yaml` shows the
  alternative: one `CommandFrame` message with a `strict` enum field.
- Responses carry no type id. On I2C, each read is one reply: decode it with `Measurement::decode(bytes)` (no
  protocol needed). The fixed-size protocols are only useful when replies arrive on a byte stream.

```cpp
// Talk to a Sensirion SHT4x over I2C: encode commands, decode the 6-byte responses (with per-word CRC-8).
// The I2C transfers are simulated with captured bytes; replace i2c_write / i2c_read with your bus driver.
#include <array>
#include <cstdio>

#include "sht4x.gmp.hpp"

namespace sht = sensirion::sht4x;

namespace {

void print_bytes(const char* what, gmsg::bytes_view b) {
    std::printf("%-8s", what);
    for (auto x : b) std::printf(" %02X", x);
    std::printf("\n");
}

}  // namespace

int main() {
    std::array<std::uint8_t, 6> tx{};

    // 1. Command: measure T & RH with high precision (write 1 byte to 0x44, then wait 8.3 ms).
    const auto n = sht::MeasureHighPrecision{}.encode(tx);
    print_bytes("write", gmsg::bytes_view(tx.data(), *n));

    // 2. Response: 6 bytes read back = T word, CRC, RH word, CRC.
    const std::array<std::uint8_t, 6> rx{0x66, 0x66, 0x93, 0x7A, 0xE1, 0xA4};
    print_bytes("read", rx);
    auto m = sht::MeasurementResponse::decode(rx);
    if (!m) {
        std::printf("bad response: %s\n", gmsg::to_string(m.error()).data());
        return 1;
    }
    const auto& meas = std::get<sht::Measurement>(*m);
    std::printf("T = %.2f degC (%.2f degF), RH = %.2f %%RH\n", meas.temperature_scaled(), meas.temperature_degf(),
                meas.humidity_scaled());

    // A corrupted byte is caught by the word CRC.
    auto bad = rx;
    bad[1] ^= 0x01;
    std::printf("corrupted: %s\n", gmsg::to_string(sht::MeasurementResponse::parse(bad).error()).data());

    // 3. Serial number (command 0x89, then read 6 bytes), using the zero-copy view.
    const std::array<std::uint8_t, 6> serial_rx{0x0F, 0x4F, 0x0B, 0x5A, 0x3C, 0x30};
    if (auto s = sht::SerialNumberView::from(serial_rx)) {
        // serial() is a computed value: (serial_high << 16) | serial_low, declared in the schema.
        std::printf("serial = 0x%08X\n", static_cast<unsigned>(s->serial()));
    }

    // The struct can also set it: set_serial() splits the value back into serial_high / serial_low.
    sht::SerialNumber sn{};
    sn.set_serial(0x0F4F5A3C);
    if (auto k = sn.encode(tx)) print_bytes("serial", gmsg::bytes_view(tx.data(), *k));

    // Encoding a response (e.g. for a sensor simulator) writes the CRCs automatically.
    sht::Measurement sim{};
    sim.set_temperature_scaled(25.0);
    sim.set_humidity_scaled(54.0);
    if (auto k = sim.encode(tx)) print_bytes("encoded", gmsg::bytes_view(tx.data(), *k));
    return 0;
}
```


## 5. Reserved sync byte with byte stuffing

**Use when:** a link where a byte value (here 0x80) may only mark the start of a frame, so every other occurrence must be escaped.

```yaml
# examples/reserved_sync/motor_link.yaml
# A serial motor-controller link where 0x80 is reserved as the sync byte.
#
# 0x80 marks the start of a frame and never appears anywhere else on the wire. Any 0x80 in the
# header, payload or CRC is replaced by two bytes: the escape byte 0x81 and the index of the
# reserved byte in the `reserved` list. The escape byte must be reserved as well:
#
#   0x80 -> 81 00
#   0x81 -> 81 01
#
# Frame (before escaping):  80 | type len | payload (len bytes) | crc16
#
# Because 0x80 cannot appear inside a frame, a receiver that sees 0x80 always knows a new frame
# starts there: a frame cut short by a dropped byte or a reset is abandoned immediately, instead
# of swallowing part of the next frame.
schema_version: 1
namespace: motor
defaults: { endian: big }

enums:
  Direction: { type: u8, strict: true, values: { forward: 0, reverse: 1 } }

messages:
  SetSpeed:
    type_id: 0x01
    doc: Host -> controller. Ramp to a new speed.
    fields:
      - { name: rpm, type: u16 }
      - { name: direction, type: Direction }
      - { name: ramp_ms, type: u16 }

  Telemetry:
    type_id: 0x02
    doc: Controller -> host, sent every 10 ms.
    fields:
      - { name: seq, type: u16 }
      - { name: rpm, type: u16 }
      - { name: current, type: u16, scale: 0.01, unit: A }
      - { name: temperature, type: i16, scale: 0.1, unit: degC }

  Log:
    type_id: 0x03
    doc: Controller -> host. Free text diagnostics.
    fields:
      - { name: len, type: u8 }
      - { name: text, type: string, length: len, max: 64 }

protocols:
  MotorLink:
    header:
      - { name: type, type: u8 }
      - { name: len, type: u8 }
    framing:
      type: length_prefixed
      sync: [0x80]
      length: { field: len, covers: body }          # payload bytes, counted before escaping
                                                    # (add `counts: wire` if your link counts escaped bytes)
      escape: { char: 0x81, code: index, reserved: [0x80, 0x81] }
    checksum: { algo: crc16_ccitt, covers: header_body }   # computed before escaping
    message_type: { field: type }
    messages: [SetSpeed, Telemetry, Log]
```

- `escape: { char: 0x81, code: index, reserved: [0x80, 0x81] }`: 0x80 → `81 00`, 0x81 → `81 01`.
- Lengths count unescaped bytes; add `counts: wire` to `length` if the device counts escaped bytes
  (only with `covers: body` or `body_checksum`).
- A raw 0x80 inside a frame means it was cut short: it is dropped (`BadDelimiter`) and parsing restarts there.
- Escaped protocols unescape in place: `parse()` takes a mutable buffer.

```cpp
// 0x80 is reserved as the sync byte: every 0x80 / 0x81 inside a frame is sent as 81 00 / 81 01.
// Encode a few frames, show the escaping, then cut one frame short and let the stream parser
// resynchronise on the next 0x80.
#include <cstdio>
#include <vector>

#include "motor_link.gmp.hpp"

namespace {

using Link = motor::MotorLink;
using Frame = std::vector<std::uint8_t>;

template <class M>
Frame encode(const M& msg) {
    std::array<std::uint8_t, Link::max_frame> buf{};
    auto n = Link::encode(msg, buf);
    if (!n) {
        std::printf("encode failed: %s\n", gmsg::to_string(n.error()).data());
        return {};
    }
    return Frame(buf.begin(), buf.begin() + static_cast<std::ptrdiff_t>(*n));
}

/// Print a wire frame with escape pairs in brackets.
void print_wire(const char* label, const Frame& f) {
    std::printf("%-10s", label);
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < f.size(); ++i) {
        if (i > 0 && f[i] == 0x81 && i + 1 < f.size()) {
            std::printf(" [%02X %02X]", f[i], f[i + 1]);
            ++i;
        } else {
            std::printf(" %02X", f[i]);
        }
    }
    std::printf("   (%zu bytes)\n", f.size());
}

} // namespace

int main() {
    // --- encoding: reserved bytes in the payload are escaped ------------------------------------
    motor::SetSpeed cmd;
    cmd.rpm = 1920;  // 0x0780
    cmd.direction = motor::Direction::forward;
    cmd.ramp_ms = 385;  // 0x0181
    const Frame set_speed = encode(cmd);

    motor::Telemetry t;
    t.seq = 128;  // 0x0080
    t.rpm = 1920;
    t.set_current_scaled(3.21);
    t.set_temperature_scaled(38.5);  // 385 = 0x0181
    const Frame telemetry = encode(t);

    motor::Log log;
    log.text = "rpm limit reached";  // `len` is filled in automatically
    const Frame log_frame = encode(log);

    t.seq = 129;
    const Frame telemetry2 = encode(t);

    std::printf("Escaped frames (escape pairs in brackets: [81 00] = 0x80, [81 01] = 0x81):\n");
    print_wire("SetSpeed", set_speed);
    print_wire("Telemetry", telemetry);
    print_wire("Log", log_frame);

    // --- whole-buffer decoding: the frame is unescaped in place, so parse() takes a mutable buffer
    Frame copy = set_speed;
    if (auto v = Link::parse(copy); v && std::holds_alternative<motor::SetSpeedView>(*v)) {
        const auto& s = std::get<motor::SetSpeedView>(*v);
        std::printf("\nparse(): SetSpeed rpm=%u direction=%s ramp=%ums\n", s.rpm(), motor::to_string(s.direction()).data(),
                    s.ramp_ms());
    }

    // --- streaming: a frame cut short, then line noise ------------------------------------------
    std::vector<std::uint8_t> wire;
    wire.insert(wire.end(), telemetry.begin(), telemetry.end());
    wire.insert(wire.end(), log_frame.begin(), log_frame.begin() + 9);  // cut short: the rest never arrives
    wire.insert(wire.end(), telemetry2.begin(), telemetry2.end());
    wire.insert(wire.end(), {0x13, 0x37});  // line noise
    wire.insert(wire.end(), log_frame.begin(), log_frame.end());

    std::printf("\nStream of %zu bytes, fed in 3-byte chunks:\n", wire.size());
    Link::Stream<> parser;
    auto handler = gmsg::overloaded{
        [](const motor::TelemetryView& v) {
            std::printf("  Telemetry seq=%u rpm=%u current=%.2fA temperature=%.1fC\n", v.seq(), v.rpm(), v.current_scaled(),
                        v.temperature_scaled());
        },
        [](const motor::LogView& v) {
            std::printf("  Log \"%.*s\"\n", static_cast<int>(v.text().size()), v.text().data());
        },
        [](const gmsg::FrameError& e) {
            std::printf("  dropped %zu byte(s): %s\n", e.data.size(), gmsg::to_string(e.error).data());
        },
    };
    const gmsg::bytes_view all(wire);
    for (std::size_t off = 0; off < all.size(); off += 3)
        parser.feed(all.subspan(off, std::min<std::size_t>(3, all.size() - off)), handler);

    const auto& st = parser.stats();
    std::printf("frames=%u errors=%u skipped=%u\n", static_cast<unsigned>(st.frames), static_cast<unsigned>(st.frame_errors),
                static_cast<unsigned>(st.bytes_skipped));
    return 0;
}
```


## 6. Custom field codec and custom checksum

**Use when:** a field GMP cannot describe declaratively (BCD dates, packed decimals, proprietary encodings) or a non-standard checksum.

```yaml
# examples/custom_codec/meter.yaml
# Custom field codec (BCD date/time) and a custom checksum function, for C++ (cpp:) and C (c:).
schema_version: 1
namespace: meter
defaults: { endian: little }

custom:
  types:
    bcd_datetime:
      wire_size: 6
      cpp: { header: "meter_codecs.hpp", type: "meter::DateTime", decode: "meter::decode_bcd", encode: "meter::encode_bcd" }
      c: { header: "meter_codecs.h", type: "meter_datetime", decode: "meter_decode_bcd", encode: "meter_encode_bcd", print: "meter_print_datetime" }
  checksums:
    mod256:
      size: 1
      cpp: { header: "meter_codecs.hpp", function: "meter::mod256" }
      c: { header: "meter_codecs.h", function: "meter_mod256" }

messages:
  Reading:
    fields:
      - { name: timestamp, type: bcd_datetime }
      - { name: kwh, type: u32, scale: 0.01, unit: kWh }

protocols:
  MeterBus:
    framing: { type: fixed, sync: [0x68], size: 12 }
    checksum: { algo: mod256, covers: body }
    messages: [Reading]
```

- The functions are checked at compile time with a clear `static_assert` message if a signature is wrong.
- Custom-type view accessors return `gmsg::Result<T>` because your decoder can fail.

```cpp
// examples/custom_codec/meter_codecs.hpp
#pragma once
// User-supplied codecs referenced from meter.yaml.

#include <gmp/byte_reader.hpp>
#include <gmp/byte_writer.hpp>

namespace meter {

struct DateTime {
    int year = 2000, month = 1, day = 1, hour = 0, minute = 0, second = 0;
    bool operator==(const DateTime&) const = default;
};

inline int bcd(std::uint8_t b) { return (b >> 4) * 10 + (b & 0x0F); }
inline std::uint8_t to_bcd(int v) { return static_cast<std::uint8_t>(((v / 10) << 4) | (v % 10)); }

/// YY MM DD hh mm ss, BCD encoded.
inline gmsg::Result<DateTime> decode_bcd(gmsg::ByteReader& r) {
    auto b = r.read_bytes(6);
    if (!b) return gmsg::fail(b.error());
    const auto& d = *b;
    DateTime t{2000 + bcd(d[0]), bcd(d[1]), bcd(d[2]), bcd(d[3]), bcd(d[4]), bcd(d[5])};
    if (t.month < 1 || t.month > 12 || t.day < 1 || t.day > 31) return gmsg::fail(gmsg::Error::InvalidValue);
    return t;
}

inline gmsg::VoidResult encode_bcd(gmsg::ByteWriter& w, const DateTime& t) {
    for (int v : {t.year - 2000, t.month, t.day, t.hour, t.minute, t.second})
        if (auto e = w.write<std::uint8_t>(to_bcd(v)); !e) return e;
    return {};
}

/// Custom checksum: modulo-256 sum.
inline std::uint8_t mod256(gmsg::bytes_view d) {
    unsigned s = 0;
    for (auto b : d) s += b;
    return static_cast<std::uint8_t>(s);
}

} // namespace meter
```

```cpp
// A custom field decoder and a custom checksum, wired in from the schema.
#include <cstdio>

#include "meter.gmp.hpp"

int main() {
    meter::Reading r;
    r.timestamp = meter::DateTime{2026, 11, 20, 14, 30, 5};
    r.set_kwh_scaled(12345.67);

    std::array<std::uint8_t, meter::MeterBus::max_frame> frame{};
    auto n = meter::MeterBus::encode(r, frame);
    if (!n) return 1;
    std::printf("frame:");
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < *n; ++i) std::printf(" %02X", frame[i]);
    std::printf("\n");

    auto any = meter::MeterBus::parse(gmsg::bytes_view(frame.data(), *n));
    if (!any) {
        std::printf("parse failed: %s\n", gmsg::to_string(any.error()).data());
        return 1;
    }
    const auto& v = std::get<meter::ReadingView>(*any);
    const auto ts = v.timestamp();  // custom-type accessors return gmsg::Result<T>
    if (!ts) return 1;
    std::printf("%04d-%02d-%02d %02d:%02d:%02d  %.2f kWh\n", ts->year, ts->month, ts->day, ts->hour, ts->minute,
                ts->second, v.kwh_scaled());
    return 0;
}
```
